title: Piano Concerto No. 23 in A major
hook: A sunny concerto with one deeply sad slow movement at its heart.

painting.title: Mr and Mrs William Hallett (‘The Morning Walk’)
painting.pairingNote: Painted in 1785 and paid for on 4 March 1786, two days after Mozart finished the concerto, it shares the music’s light, feathery elegance and the shade at its edges.

facts: Mozart entered the concerto in his own catalogue of works on 2 March 1786, while he was busy with *The Marriage of Figaro*. It is the middle one of three piano concertos he finished that winter, and he probably played it himself at one of his Lent subscription concerts in Vienna.

The paper of the manuscript shows that he had started it in about 1784. When he came back to it, he crossed out the oboes and wrote in clarinets. The orchestra is small: one flute, two clarinets, two bassoons, two horns and strings, with no trumpets or drums.
Mozart wrote the first movement’s [[cadenza|cadenza]] straight into the score, instead of on a separate sheet as he usually did.

The slow movement is in F-sharp minor, the only movement Mozart wrote in that key. The pianist András Schiff calls it one of the most sorrowful pieces Mozart ever wrote, and it sits between two sunny movements in A major.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a warm, singing Allegro with a surprise new tune (I), a lonely lament in a swaying rhythm (II), a quick finale full of new tunes and sudden turns (III).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A gentle, singing first movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with a [[double-exposition|double exposition]]: the orchestra presents the main tunes first, and only then does the piano enter and present them again. Almost everything is soft and lyrical, but small shadows keep passing over it.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a calm tune in the violins, answered by the woodwinds. Its second chord is already slightly clouded.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a quieter, sliding melody that begins in the strings and gradually draws in bassoon and flute.

mainIdeas.name: The new theme
mainIdeas.description: a quiet tune that the orchestra keeps back until the piano has finished its exposition. The whole [[development|development]] is built on it.

stops.hear: Strings alone play a calm, even tune; after a few bars the woodwinds answer with the same tune
stops.happening: Theme 1, first heard in the orchestra. No piano yet

stops.hear: The whole orchestra comes in, louder and more energetic
stops.happening: The first [[tutti|tutti]]

stops.hear: Strings alone again with a softer, sliding melody; a bassoon and then the flute slip in
stops.happening: Theme 2, still in the home key

stops.hear: The piano enters alone with the opening tune
stops.happening: The second, solo exposition begins. Now the music will move to a new key

stops.hear: The piano starts the sliding melody, then hands it to violins, bassoon and flute and decorates it with quiet broken octaves
stops.happening: Theme 2, now in E major

stops.hear: After the piano’s trill and a burst from the orchestra, the strings play a quiet tune that has not been heard before
stops.happening: The new theme. Mozart saved it for this moment

stops.label: Mid-development
stops.hear: Woodwinds and strings pass pieces of the new tune between them while the piano plays running figures; the music slips into minor keys
stops.happening: The [[development|development]], made almost entirely from the new theme

stops.hear: The calm opening tune returns in the home key
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: The orchestra stops on a held chord and the piano plays alone, freely, ending with a long trill
stops.happening: The [[cadenza|cadenza]], written by Mozart himself

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The orchestra alone rounds off the movement
stops.happening: The closing [[tutti|tutti]]. The piano does not play again

notice: The piano waits more than two minutes before it plays a note. Listen to how quietly it enters, with the same tune the strings began with.
The new theme at about 4:50 sounds like an afterthought, but the whole middle of the movement grows out of it.

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.summary: A slow lament in F-sharp minor in a swaying [[siciliano|siciliano]] rhythm. The piano begins alone, like a singer without accompaniment, and a brighter middle section only briefly lifts the mood.

mainIdeas.name: The lament
mainIdeas.description: a slow, lilting tune for piano alone with unusually wide leaps, down and up.

mainIdeas.name: The consolation
mainIdeas.description: a brighter tune in A major, introduced by the flute and the clarinet.

stops.hear: The piano alone plays a slow, rocking melody that leaps far down and back up
stops.happening: The main theme, in F-sharp minor

stops.hear: The orchestra answers softly; the clarinet, the violins and the bassoon follow each other and rub against each other
stops.happening: The orchestra takes up the lament. The clashing notes are deliberate

stops.hear: The mood brightens: the flute and the clarinet play a warm new tune and the piano replies
stops.happening: The middle section, in A major

stops.hear: The piano returns to the rocking minor melody
stops.happening: The opening section returns

stops.hear: Very quiet: the violins play with the bow, the lower strings pluck, and the piano’s line thins out
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. The movement fades out in the minor

notice: In the coda, only the lower strings play [[pizzicato|pizzicato]]; the violins keep their bows. Mozart’s manuscript shows this clearly, but older printed editions had all the strings plucking.

notes.title: Mozart’s own word
notes.body: The score says Adagio, a truly slow tempo that Mozart rarely asked for in his concertos. Spotify’s track list calls the movement “Andante”; that title is not Mozart’s.

movements.heading: Allegro assai
movements.summary: A fast, high-spirited finale that seems never to stop moving. It is a [[rondo|rondo]]: the piano’s opening tune keeps coming back, but in between Mozart brings in new tunes and sudden changes of key, like scene changes in a comic opera.

mainIdeas.name: The refrain
mainIdeas.description: a quick, bouncing tune that the piano plays alone first.

mainIdeas.name: The piano’s own tune
mainIdeas.description: a gentler melody the orchestra never introduced.

mainIdeas.name: Two surprises
mainIdeas.description: an episode in F-sharp minor and a clarinet tune in D major.

stops.hear: The piano alone plays a quick, bouncing tune
stops.happening: The rondo theme

stops.hear: The whole orchestra bursts in with the same tune and keeps going for almost a minute, ending on a pause
stops.happening: The opening [[tutti|tutti]]

stops.hear: The piano starts a gentler, singing tune; the clarinets answer
stops.happening: A new theme of the piano’s own

stops.hear: A plaintive minor melody in the flute and bassoon over the strings; the piano takes it up and swerves into a brighter key
stops.happening: The second theme, in E minor

stops.hear: The bouncing tune returns in the piano, but the orchestra soon steers it into the minor
stops.happening: The refrain comes back and changes direction

stops.hear: Piano figures over a bare accompaniment, answered by the woodwinds alone
stops.happening: An episode in F-sharp minor, the key of the slow movement

stops.hear: A simple, smiling tune in the clarinet and the woodwinds, the piano accompanying; then the piano plays it too
stops.happening: The surprise turn to D major

stops.hear: The piano’s gentle tune from ≈ 1:00 returns, now in the home key
stops.happening: The return section. Mozart brings the other themes back before the refrain

stops.hear: The bouncing tune returns, piano first and then the full orchestra
stops.happening: The final return of the refrain

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Piano and orchestra trade closing figures; the orchestra has the last word
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

notice: Count how many different tunes appear. Mozart keeps adding new ones where you expect the refrain.
Listen for the clarinet at about 4:05. It is the same instrument that replaced the oboes in this concerto.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Daniel Barenboim plays the piano and directs the Berlin Philharmonic from the keyboard, with no separate conductor.

threads.title: Clarinets
threads.body: Mozart swapped the oboes for clarinets, and they colour every movement: answering the first theme, bringing the light in the Adagio, and leading the surprise tune in the finale.

threads.title: The piano starts alone
threads.body: In the first movement the piano waits for the orchestra to finish. In the second and third, it begins on its own.

threads.title: F-sharp minor
threads.body: The key of the slow movement comes back as a shadow in the middle of the finale.
